name: Kudzu

facts.what: Grape-scented purple flowers; young leaves; starchy root
facts.how: Flowers into jelly and tea; young leaves cooked
facts.where: Smothering East Texas roadsides and woods edges
facts.value: The flowers are fragrant and edible

caution: A safe and famously invasive plant to harvest freely; just gather away from roadside spray. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: The vine that ate the South, blanketing everything it climbs. In late summer it hangs clusters of purple flowers that smell of grape soda.

sections.title: Uses
sections.body: The flowers make a startling purple jelly and a fragrant tea; young leaves cook like any green, and the root is a traditional starch.
